history.summary: CSV town 'Lohardaga' corrected to the actual village, Khakparta (8 km from Lohardaga). An ancient east-facing Rekha Deul (Nagara-style) Shiva temple built directly on the hilltop rock surface with no foundation, about 4 m high with a triratha plan and ornamental shikhara; a 1-metre-high narrow entrance leads to the garbhagriha housing a Shivlinga, with Ganesha, Surya and Nandi idols in front. Archaeological excavations in the early 2000s uncovered eight more 3-m temples (seven with Shivlingas) at the foothill; the Archaeological Survey of India protects the site and was renovating the excavated temples. One of the rarest surviving 9th-10th century temples in Jharkhand. There is no priest and no regular worship.

name: Prachin Shiv Mandir, Khakparta
town_description: Khakparta is a village in Lohardaga Sadar block, about 8 km from Lohardaga town in Jharkhand's bauxite-rich plateau country. The ancient Shiva temple sits atop a small hill above the village, offering panoramic views of Khakparta, neighbouring Rampur village, a large pond and fields. It is listed by the district administration as one of Lohardaga's most popular visitor spots.

travel.railway: Lohardaga railway station, ~8 km; connected to Ranchi and Tori
travel.road: ~8 km from Lohardaga via Haramu/Bhakso; ~90 km northwest of Ranchi; accessible by a flight of about a hundred steps to the hilltop
